# Hundred-Day Plan

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. A good first-hundred-days plan protects value, it does not create a guarantee: portfolio companies can still underperform or lose money, there is a real risk of loss, and no plan here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the hundred-day plan skill of the private equity pack in andreworia/claude-finance-skills. Use it between signing and completion, when the team converts the investment thesis into what actually happens after the wire clears; it applies equally to a carve-out carrying TSA obligations and to a bolt-on where the hundred days belong to integration, and it exists to fix the classic failure mode, a draft that already runs to thirty actions. The method budgets bandwidth before choosing any moves: count the executive-days genuinely available (executives who can carry change work, times fourteen weeks, times the share of their week not spent running the business, usually one day in five), and treat any plan costing more than that budget as a wish list. It then chooses three to five moves only, each of which must protect value acquired, unlock a named lever in the EBITDA bridge, or buy information diligence could not, prices each in executive-days and holds back about 20 percent because something unforecast always arrives in month one.
